correctness.rationale: For a rank-r matrix A with weak-Schatten norm one, Ky Fan bounds the kth diagonal modulus by H_min(k,r)(q)/k. The Laplace integral proves k^(q-1) H_k(q) strictly increases for every q>0; the upper envelope therefore maximizes at n if q>1, at r if q<1, and all k>=r if q=1. Fourier-conjugated harmonic spectra attain each value. Saturation of the diagonal trace-norm bound forces the exact harmonic singular spectrum and diagonal-unitary times positive semidefinite form, giving all equality cases. Verified finite checker: 22604 checks; universal proof does not rely on diagnostics.

value.rationale: Canonical diagonal pinching is the central pattern in the recent qualitative classification of Schur-bounded quasi-Banach ideals. The exact n/r/p invariant sharply distinguishes polynomial dimension amplification by rank-one matrices for p<1, logarithmic rank-dependent amplification at p=1, and dimension-uniform bounds for p>1; it also locates a complete jump in extremal coordinate support and determines every equality matrix. Thus the rank budget is motivated by the minimum matrix complexity needed to witness failure of weak-ideal boundedness, not an arbitrary numerical slice. This is a self-contained exact classification, not merely a known boundedness verdict.
